name: Shopify
oneLiner: Multi-store apps need Shopify App Store review

review.what: Shopify App Store review (public distribution), plus protected customer data review if you read customer data

cost.text: One-time $19 USD App Store registration fee per Partner account

limits.text: Before approval: a custom-distribution app installs only on one store, stores in one Plus organization, or development stores.
Before approval: protected customer data needs no review only while the app is installed solely on development stores.

requirements.text: Public apps must request protected customer data access, and level 1 and 2 access requires review.
App Store apps must subscribe to the customers/data_request, customers/redact and shop/redact compliance webhooks.
New public apps must be built only with the GraphQL Admin API.
Review submissions need a screencast, working test credentials and an emergency developer contact.
The app must authenticate with OAuth immediately after install, before any other step.
App charges must go through Shopify App Pricing or the Billing API.

gotchas.text: Composio has no managed Shopify app, so you must bring your own credentials.
New public apps must use expiring offline tokens that last 1 hour, with refresh tokens valid 90 days.
You cannot change the distribution method after you select it.
Composio asks for the store subdomain (e.g. je0xpi-12) when connecting an account.
Order updates can 403 without the read_all_orders scope.

steps.t: Create an app in the Shopify Dev Dashboard, set the app URL and scopes
Add the Composio redirect URI, release the version, copy Client ID and secret
Create a Composio auth config with your own Shopify credentials
Choose public distribution and pay the $19 App Store registration fee
Draft data-use justifications for protected customer data access
Add compliance webhooks, screencast and test credentials, then submit for review

unverified: Shopify does not publish an App Store review duration.
Portal URL partners.shopify.com not fetched; Composio's guide starts from the Dev Dashboard in Shopify Admin.

name: Xero
oneLiner: Uncertified apps cap at 50 orgs; free tier caps at 5

review.what: Xero app certification (required for the Plus tier and above, over 50 connections)

cost.text: Starter free (5 connections); Core $35 AUD/mo (50); Plus $245 AUD/mo (1,000), tax exclusive

limits.text: Before certification: new apps start on Starter with 5 connections, and Core allows up to 50.
Each Xero organisation can connect at most five uncertified apps.
Starter allows 1,000 API calls per day per organisation; higher tiers allow 5,000.
All tiers: 60 calls per minute and 5 concurrent calls per organisation.

requirements.text: Plus, Advanced and Enterprise tiers require app certification.
Core and above require a payment method on file.
Certification requires the offline_access scope.
Certification needs a connect/disconnect settings page showing the connected tenant name and status.
The app name cannot include the word Xero.
Listing on the Xero App Store requires the Plus tier or higher.

gotchas.text: Composio has no managed Xero app, so you must bring your own credentials.
Data from Xero's APIs may not be used to train AI/ML models.
Access tokens last 30 minutes; refresh tokens last 60 days and rotate on each use.
Apps created on or after 2 March 2026 use Xero's new granular scopes.
Redirect URI must use https with no trailing slash.

steps.t: Create a Web app at developer.xero.com with the Composio redirect URI
Copy the Client ID and generate a client secret
Create a Composio auth config with your own Xero credentials and scopes
Add a payment method to move to Core if you need more than 5 connections
Check your integration against Xero's certification checkpoints
Submit for certification before you pass 50 connections

callbackNote: Add Composio's redirect URI https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback (https, no trailing slash).
unverified: Xero does not publish how long certification takes.
Granular scope names were not checked against Composio's default Xero scopes.

name: QuickBooks Online
oneLiner: Production keys need an approved app assessment

review.what: Intuit App Assessment Questionnaire, approved before production keys are shown

cost.text: $0 on the Builder tier; Silver is $300 USD/month

limits.text: Before approval: you only have development keys; the production Show Credentials switch stays hidden.
Builder tier: 500,000 CorePlus API calls per month, and calls above that are blocked.

requirements.text: Production app details need EULA and privacy policy URLs, host domain, launch, disconnect and connect/reconnect URLs.
Production redirect URIs must use https, and IP addresses are not allowed.
You must get the App Assessment Questionnaire approved to see production credentials.
Listed apps must be on the Silver tier or above to avoid delisting.

gotchas.text: Access tokens last 1 hour; refresh tokens expire after 100 days unused.
The refresh token value rotates every 24 hours, so always store the latest one.
Refresh tokens have a hard limit of 5 years, after which users must reconnect.
Development and production keys are separate, and sandbox redirect URIs can use localhost.
The com.intuit.quickbooks.payment scope can cause Cloudflare Error 1016 if Payments is not enabled.
Sandbox connections need https://sandbox-quickbooks.api.intuit.com as the base URL in Composio.
The Intuit App Partner Program is available only to partners in the US, UK, Australia and Canada (excluding Quebec).

steps.t: Create an app in the Intuit Developer Portal and add the Composio redirect URI
Draft the EULA and privacy policy pages
Fill in production App Details (URLs, categories, hosting regions)
Test connect, disconnect and reconnect with a sandbox company
Complete the App Assessment Questionnaire under Production > Compliance
Create a Composio auth config with the production Client ID and secret

callbackNote: Add Composio's redirect URI https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback to the Production redirect URIs tab (https only).
unverified: Intuit does not state how long questionnaire review takes.
The 40-minute questionnaire estimate is ours, not Intuit's.
Portal URL path not confirmed; docs say My Hub > App dashboard.

name: Stripe
oneLiner: Connect OAuth is legacy; Stripe Apps review takes 4 days

review.what: No review in Stripe's Connect OAuth setup docs; Stripe Apps need App Marketplace review

cost.text: No fee stated for Connect OAuth or Stripe Apps setup

limits.text: Connect OAuth with read_write cannot connect to Standard accounts controlled by another platform.
Stripe Apps before publishing: external testing is capped at 25 testers per app.

requirements.text: Each redirect URI must be listed in Connect OAuth settings, and live mode redirect URIs must use HTTPS.
Stripe Apps review needs test credentials, testing guidance and the live-mode public install URL.
Your business cannot be on Stripe's prohibited and restricted businesses list to publish an app.

gotchas.text: Stripe says OAuth is not recommended for new Connect platforms.
New Connect extensions can no longer be built; Stripe Apps replaced them.
Only extensions can use the read_only scope, so new platforms get read_write.
The Connect token call uses your platform's secret API key as client_secret.
Each client_id is either live or test, so use the matching one per environment.
Stripe Apps OAuth access tokens expire in 1 hour; refresh tokens last 1 year and roll on use.

steps.t: In the Stripe Dashboard, enable OAuth under Connect onboarding options
Add the Composio redirect URI and copy the ca_ client_id
Create a Composio auth config with the client_id and your secret key
Test with a test-mode client_id before switching to live
Check whether you need Stripe Apps OAuth instead, given Connect OAuth is not recommended

callbackNote: Add Composio's redirect URI https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback to your Connect OAuth redirect URIs (HTTPS in live mode).

sources.t: Stripe OAuth changes for Standard platforms

unverified: Composio's own-credentials guide uses Connect OAuth; whether Composio accepts Stripe Apps OAuth credentials is not documented.
Whether a Connect platform needs Stripe review before live-mode OAuth was not confirmed.
Composio's guide suggests read_only,read_write scopes, which conflicts with Stripe limiting read_only to extensions.

name: Dropbox
oneLiner: Apply for production within 2 weeks of 50 users

review.wait: not stated; review starts after 50 linked users

limits.text: Before approval: a development app links only your own account until you click Enable additional users.
Before approval: a development app can link at most 500 Dropbox users.
After 50 linked users you have two weeks to get production approval, or new links are frozen.

requirements.text: The app must follow Dropbox's branding guidelines and terms, or production is rejected.
Request the least privileged permissions; Dropbox reviews scope breadth at production.
The production application asks how the app uses the API and for an app icon.
The app name cannot include Dropbox, start with drop, or use DBX or DB.

gotchas.text: Production review does not start until 50 linked users unless you request early review.
A frozen app can only be unfrozen by getting production approval, not by unlinking users.
You cannot change the app name after production approval.
Access tokens are short-lived; add token_access_type=offline to get a refresh token.
Redirect URIs must exactly match a registered value in the App Console.

steps.t: Create a Scoped access app in the Dropbox App Console
Add the Composio redirect URI and enable only needed permissions
Create a Composio auth config with the app key and secret
Click Enable additional users so others can connect
Draft the production application describing API use
Apply for production status before or soon after 50 users

callbackNote: Add Composio's redirect URI https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback under OAuth 2 Redirect URIs.
unverified: Dropbox does not publish how long production review takes.

name: Box
oneLiner: No review needed, but some enterprises must enable it

review.what: Optional Box Partner team review to list in Box Integrations

limits.text: If an enterprise turns on Disable unpublished apps by default, its admin must enable your OAuth 2.0 app first.

requirements.text: Redirect URIs must be HTTPS, or HTTP only for localhost or loopback addresses.
Box Integrations listing accepts only OAuth 2.0 apps that are finished and production-ready.

gotchas.text: You cannot change the authentication method after creating the app.
Refresh tokens are single-use and expire after 60 days, after which users must re-authorize.
Admins enable an OAuth 2.0 app by entering its client ID under Platform > Platform Apps.
Box disables all unpublished platform apps when that enterprise setting is on.
Redirect URIs are checked by exact match.

steps.t: In the Box Developer Console, create a Platform App with User Authentication (OAuth 2.0)
Add the Composio redirect URI and select scopes on the Configuration tab
Create a Composio auth config with your Box client ID and secret
Write admin instructions for enabling your client ID in enterprise accounts
Optionally submit the app for Box Integrations from the Publishing tab

callbackNote: Add Composio's redirect URI https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback (HTTPS, exact match).

sources.t: Box support: Enterprise settings, platform apps

unverified: developer.box.com did not resolve from this environment; Box facts come from Box's official docs repo on GitHub, which may lag the live site.
Box does not state how long Box Integrations review takes.
Composio has no Box own-credentials guide; portal URL app.box.com/developers/console not fetched.
